item.content:encoded:
Each reading is based on a fixed rashi tarot anchor and a six-card daily spread covering overall energy, love, career, money, health, and spiritual guidance.
MESHA RASHI / ARIESToday's Theme:
Pause before the leap, today's energy works best with courage plus better timing.
Best Area:
Career feels smoother when creativity and diplomacy lead the conversation.
Watch Out For:
Money temptations and sharp words can create avoidable stress today.
Card Reading:
The Emperor is your fixed anchor, while today's overall card, The Fool reversed, turns bold leadership toward caution, timing, and self-control. For Mesha, the day isn't about stopping action, it's about checking where impulse or hesitation is distorting the next move.
General | Card: The Fool reversed
You're ready to move fast, but the day works better when you slow the first step. The Fool reversed can feel like one part of you wants a fresh start while another part keeps second-guessing it. That can create stop-start energy, especially during a commute or while replying to a pending message. Keep plans simple. Don't announce too much too early. Progress comes from checking details, not from dramatic moves.
If something feels exciting and risky at once, give it a second look before saying yes.
Love and Relationship | Card: King of Swords reversed
Conversations in close relationships need extra care today. With King of Swords reversed in love, blunt truth can easily turn into coldness, or someone else's words may feel controlling. If you're waiting on a WhatsApp reply, don't build a full story from silence. Couples should avoid turning a small issue into a courtroom debate. Singles may meet someone intelligent yet emotionally unavailable, so stay observant. Clear words matter, but tone matters just as much. Say what you mean without trying to win.
Education and Career | Card: Knight of Cups upright
Work gets a softer, more imaginative flow through Knight of Cups upright. A client call, pitch, creative task, or even a difficult follow-up can go better when you bring charm instead of force. People respond to sincerity today. If you've been pushing too hard, change the approach and make the message more human. Students also do well with subjects that need expression and interpretation, not just speed. A good idea may arrive in a quiet moment, so note it before the rush returns.
Money and Finance | Card: The Devil upright
Money needs strong boundaries today. The Devil upright can pull attention toward compulsive spending, status pressure, or holding on too tightly to something that isn't useful anymore. Check that online shopping cart before you hit pay. A UPI payment made in haste may not be the best choice. This isn't a bad money day, but it is one where habits speak loudly. Keep your budget visible, avoid emotional purchases, and don't let urgency decide for you.
Health and Well-being | Card: Page of Cups upright
Your wellbeing improves through gentleness, not intensity. Page of Cups upright connects health with emotional softness, hydration, and small comforting routines. If your mood has been jumpy, a lighter schedule and better food timing can help. Give yourself a little breathing space between tasks. Music, journaling, or even a calmer lunch break may restore more energy than a power push today.
Spiritual Guidance | Card: Six of Wands upright
Six of Wands upright reminds you that right action builds quiet confidence. Spiritual strength grows when you notice where you've already handled things better than before. Stand before your prayer corner for one minute and let that small inner victory register.
VRISHABHA RASHI / TAURUSToday's Theme:
Home, stability, and long-term thinking feel strong, even if work shifts suddenly.
Best Area:
Love supports steady growth through practical effort and sincere consistency.
Watch Out For:
Career surprises may test your comfort zone and fixed expectations.
Card Reading:
The Hierophant is your fixed anchor, while today's overall card, Ten of Pentacles upright, deepens the focus on stability, family ties, and lasting value. For Vrishabha, familiar structures feel supportive today, though comfort must stay flexible enough to handle change elsewhere.
General | Card: Ten of Pentacles upright
The day carries a grounded, family-linked tone. Ten of Pentacles upright puts attention on long-term security, shared responsibilities, and what truly lasts. You may think more about home matters, future planning, or how your daily choices affect the bigger picture. A family dinner conversation or even a practical discussion about household routines can be more meaningful than usual. This is good energy for strengthening foundations, but don't confuse stability with standing still. What lasts grows through care, not just habit.
Love and Relationship | Card: Page of Pentacles upright
Love feels steady and sincere. Page of Pentacles upright brings a simple, dependable tone, where effort matters more than drama. If you're in a relationship, practical gestures, showing up on time, remembering something important, helping with a task, all count. Singles may notice interest growing slowly through shared routine, work, or study rather than instant sparks. Keep expectations realistic and warm. A connection can deepen through patience. Small consistency today may do more than a big emotional speech.
Education and Career | Card: The Tower upright
Work may not stay predictable, and that's where the lesson sits. The Tower upright can bring a sudden update, a changed plan, an HR email, or a truth you can no longer ignore. It may feel disruptive first, especially if you like a steady method, but the shake-up can clear what wasn't solid. Don't react from panic or pride. Read carefully, ask direct questions, and adapt step by step. What changes now may help you build on firmer ground later.
Money and Finance | Card: King of Wands upright
Money matters benefit from confidence and initiative. King of Wands upright is strong for taking charge of budgeting, pricing, or a practical business idea. If a pending payment needs chasing, do it directly. You may also feel motivated to think bigger about income, but keep the fire balanced with facts. This is better for leadership in financial matters than for reckless spending. Make the call, send the reminder, and act like the adult in the room.
Health and Well-being | Card: Knight of Cups reversed
Emotions can quietly affect energy levels today. Knight of Cups reversed often shows mood-driven routine, irregular rest, or expecting yourself to feel inspired before taking care of basics. Don't wait for the perfect mood. Eat on time, hydrate, and reduce emotional overthinking before sleep. If the heart feels heavy, keep the body routine simple and steady.
Spiritual Guidance | Card: Two of Cups upright
Two of Cups upright turns your spiritual focus toward harmony, not isolation. A kind exchange, shared prayer, or honest listening can become part of your inner practice today. Ask yourself quietly, where am I ready to meet life halfway?
MITHUNA RASHI / GEMINIToday's Theme:
Your mind may feel crowded, but warmth and clarity are still available.
Best Area:
Love flows best through care, softness, and emotionally present communication.
Watch Out For:
Overloaded money duties can pile up if you keep saying yes.
Card Reading:
The Lovers is your fixed anchor, while today's overall card, Eight of Swords upright, narrows the mind with doubt, overthinking, or self-made pressure. For Mithuna, choice and connection remain central, but today's lesson is to loosen mental knots before making everything more complicated.
General | Card: Eight of Swords upright
Your thoughts may run in circles today, and that can make small matters feel bigger than they are. Eight of Swords upright often shows mental crowding, where too many options become their own trap. If you're stuck between messages, plans, or opinions, reduce the noise. Don't answer every chat immediately, and don't turn one delay into a full problem. Even during the metro rush, one clear decision is better than five half-decisions. The day improves when you stop feeding the loop and choose one practical next step.
Love and Relationship | Card: The Empress upright
Love has a much softer tone than your thoughts do. The Empress upright brings warmth, affection, and a fuller emotional presence. If you're partnered, care can be shown through comfort, patience, and making space for each other's real feelings. Singles may attract someone grounded, affectionate, and genuine. This isn't about clever lines. It's about emotional availability. A meal shared, a kind check-in, or thoughtful attention can deepen connection more than constant talking. Let tenderness do some of the work today.
Education and Career | Card: Three of Cups upright
Work benefits from people, not solo pressure. Three of Cups upright is excellent for teamwork, networking, group study, and collaborative wins. An office chai break may bring a useful idea or the right introduction. If you've been carrying a task alone, involve others where possible. Students also do better with discussion and shared revision than isolated stress. Keep the tone light but focused. A cheerful exchange can open a practical door, and group energy may help you finish what felt mentally blocked earlier.
Money and Finance | Card: Ten of Wands upright
Financially, the load may feel heavier than usual. Ten of Wands upright suggests bills, duties, or too many small commitments stacking up at once. Rent, subscriptions, or family expenses may need sorting without drama. The answer isn't avoidance, it's prioritising. Write down what must be handled first and what can wait. If you're carrying someone else's financial burden too often, notice that pattern. Responsible action helps, but don't act like every expense is yours alone to fix.
Health and Well-being | Card: Six of Pentacles upright
Balance is the main message for wellbeing. Six of Pentacles upright connects health with fair energy exchange, giving your body proper food, rest, movement, and breaks instead of taking from it all day. If you've been mentally generous with everyone except yourself, correct that. Regular meals, posture care, and sharing workload where possible will help your energy settle.
Spiritual Guidance | Card: The Sun upright
The Sun upright clears inner fog through honesty and simple joy. Spiritual strength today doesn't need complexity, it needs openness. End the day with one grateful thought for what is already working in your life.
KARKA RASHI / CANCERToday's Theme:
Clear words and firm emotional boundaries help you move the day with more confidence.
Best Area:
Career feels fresh and promising, especially where learning and initiative matter most.
Watch Out For:
Relationship moods may swing if you resist an overdue emotional adjustment.
Card Reading:
The Chariot is your anchor, while today's overall card, Queen of Swords upright, asks Cancerian feeling to travel with sharper judgment, cleaner boundaries, and honest speech. Heart and head work best together when sensitivity stays steady, not defensive or withdrawn.
General | Card: Queen of Swords upright
Today works better when you stop guessing and start saying things plainly. Queen of Swords upright gives your naturally protective side a cleaner edge, so you can handle family, work, and personal plans without carrying everyone else's mood. If a WhatsApp reply has been delayed or a family dinner topic feels awkward, direct but calm words will help more than silence. Keep your standards clear. You don't need to explain yourself ten times. One mature conversation can save you a lot of emotional drain later in the day.
Love and Relationship | Card: Wheel of Fortune reversed
Love may feel slightly off rhythm today, and Wheel of Fortune reversed suggests resistance to a needed shift. If you're waiting for someone to behave exactly as before, frustration can build. Couples may notice repeating patterns around timing, attention, or emotional availability. Singles could feel tired of mixed signals. Don't call it bad luck, call it a cycle that needs awareness. A softer tone helps, but so does realism. Let the connection breathe instead of forcing certainty before it's ready.
Education and Career | Card: Page of Wands upright
Work and study matters get a lift from Page of Wands upright. There's room for a new idea, a fresh assignment, or a learning curve that actually excites you. If a boss follow-up lands suddenly, handle it with curiosity instead of pressure. This card favours initiative, pitching, applying, drafting, and starting before you feel fully ready. Cancer energy can hesitate when emotions are unsettled, but today's momentum improves once you take the first step. Keep it simple, stay open, and let enthusiasm carry the task forward.
Money and Finance | Card: Seven of Pentacles upright
Money needs patience, not panic. Seven of Pentacles upright is steady energy for reviewing where your effort is going and whether returns are taking time rather than failing altogether. A pending payment, savings goal, or household expense may need another round of practical planning. This isn't the best mood for impulsive spending just because progress feels slow. Track what you've already built. Small consistency matters more than quick results today, especially if you're balancing family needs with your own future security.
Health and Well-being | Card: Knight of Cups upright
Your wellbeing is closely tied to emotional flow today. Knight of Cups upright points to gentler energy, better hydration, slower meals, and softer self-talk. If your mood changes with the commute or home atmosphere, don't ignore it. Choose routines that help you feel settled, not rushed. Music, quiet time, and lighter food can support balance. Rest isn't laziness today, it's how you protect your energy from becoming heavy or reactive.
Spiritual Guidance | Card: Strength upright
Strength upright reminds you that real control is calm, not force. Your inner life grows when compassion and restraint stay together, especially during emotionally charged moments. Spend a minute at your prayer corner and breathe before reacting. Quiet strength changes the whole tone of the day.
SIMHA RASHI / LEOToday's Theme:
You're moving out of old disappointment and finding steadier emotional ground by evening.
Best Area:
Career flows best through calm leadership, tact, and emotionally balanced decision-making.
Watch Out For:
Home or relationship expectations may trigger drama if flexibility is missing.
Card Reading:
Strength is your anchor, while today's overall card, Five of Cups reversed, turns pride toward healing, acceptance, and emotional recovery. Leo's warmth shines best now through grace after disappointment, not through replaying what didn't work.
General | Card: Five of Cups reversed
A weight begins to lift today. Five of Cups reversed suggests you're ready to stop feeding an old hurt, regret, or disappointment, even if the memory hasn't fully gone. That shift matters. For Leo, emotional recovery often starts when self-respect returns without the need to prove anything. If the morning chai tastes quieter than usual, take that as a sign you're processing well, not losing sparkle. Let the day be about what can still be repaired, enjoyed, or continued. Peace doesn't reduce your fire, it steadies it.
Love and Relationship | Card: Four of Wands reversed
Love needs less performance and more adjustment. Four of Wands reversed can bring minor disharmony around home routines, plans, or how secure a bond feels right now. A partner may seem unavailable, or family involvement may complicate the mood. If you're single, attraction may be there but timing feels awkward. Don't turn one missed plan into a bigger story. A family dinner conversation could easily become touchy if expectations stay rigid. Keep warmth in the room, but lower the pressure for everything to feel perfect.
Education and Career | Card: King of Cups upright
Career is the strongest zone today. King of Cups upright helps you lead through emotional control, maturity, and smart handling of people. If you're dealing with a client call, team issue, or sensitive office matter, your tone matters as much as your content. Others respond well when you stay composed instead of dramatic. This is good energy for managers, teachers, freelancers, and anyone needing trust. You don't have to dominate the room. Calm authority will do more for your reputation than a loud display of confidence.
Money and Finance | Card: Three of Wands upright
Money matters benefit from foresight today. Three of Wands upright supports planning ahead, thinking bigger, and making decisions that look beyond this week's spending. You may review an EMI, future purchase, or a possible income expansion with better clarity. This card favours preparation over impulse. If something looks promising, research it before committing. If something is delayed, use the gap wisely. Financial confidence grows when your choices reflect vision, not just mood or image.
Health and Well-being | Card: Nine of Swords reversed
Stress levels can improve if you stop carrying everything alone. Nine of Swords reversed is good for recovery from overthinking, disturbed sleep, or mental pressure that has been lingering. Cut late-night screen time and don't keep replaying one awkward moment. If needed, talk it out during an office chai break or with someone you trust. Your system responds well today to rest, lighter thoughts, and a little emotional honesty.
Spiritual Guidance | Card: Two of Pentacles upright
Two of Pentacles upright reminds you that balance is also a sacred practice. Daily duties, emotional needs, and personal pride all need fair space. What are you juggling well, and what are you pretending is still under control?
KANYA RASHI / VIRGOToday's Theme:
A mental knot loosens when you stop over-correcting and allow a simpler way forward.
Best Area:
Health and routine feel most supportive through moderation, pacing, and steady habits.
Watch Out For:
Career chatter or half-baked information could waste time if not verified.
Card Reading:
The Hermit is your anchor, while today's overall card, Eight of Swords reversed, releases some self-made pressure around getting everything exactly right. Virgo's insight becomes more useful now when reflection leads to action, not another loop of analysis.
General | Card: Eight of Swords reversed
You may notice relief today the moment you stop assuming you're stuck. Eight of Swords reversed opens a door that was always there, but stress or perfectionism may have made it hard to see. Plans can move once you drop one limiting thought, one unnecessary apology, or one impossible standard. During the metro rush or between tasks, a new perspective can arrive suddenly. Don't overprocess it. This is a good day to simplify, unfreeze, and act on what already makes sense. Freedom starts with one practical decision, not a dramatic breakthrough.
Love and Relationship | Card: Eight of Pentacles upright
Love grows through effort, not mind reading. Eight of Pentacles upright is steady relationship energy for improving communication, showing up properly, and giving attention to the small things that build trust. If you're committed, shared routines matter more than grand gestures today. If you're single, someone consistent may impress you more than someone flashy. Even a thoughtful tiffin packed with care or a checked-in message can mean a lot. Keep expectations realistic and effort mutual. Slow progress in love is still progress.
Education and Career | Card: Page of Swords reversed
Work needs sharp filtering today. Page of Swords reversed can bring gossip, incomplete facts, overthinking, or someone speaking before they know enough. If an HR email, office update, or study-related message seems unclear, verify details before reacting. Virgo energy is good at catching errors, but don't let suspicion become its own distraction. Keep your communication crisp and avoid promising what isn't ready. Research is useful, but endless checking isn't. The smartest move today is informed restraint, especially if others are being noisy or careless.
Money and Finance | Card: Six of Wands reversed
Money confidence may feel lower than the actual situation. Six of Wands reversed can make you compare your progress with others or feel unnoticed for your effort. Avoid spending to prove success, whether through online shopping cart temptation or image-based choices. This card suits a quieter review of where your resources are going and what results are realistic. Recognition may be delayed, but that doesn't make your planning weak. Stay practical, skip the ego spend, and let consistency speak later.
Health and Well-being | Card: Temperance upright
Your body and mind respond best to moderation today. Temperance upright supports balanced meals, proper water intake, steadier timing, and not swinging between overwork and total collapse. If your study timetable or daily routine has become extreme, soften it. Gentle discipline works better than pressure. This is good energy for recovery through pacing, lighter food, and calmer transitions between tasks. The more even your rhythm, the better your energy holds.
Spiritual Guidance | Card: King of Wands reversed
Inner guidance gets distorted when control becomes ego. King of Wands reversed asks for one honest correction in how you're directing your will. You don't need to push life so hard. I release the need to force what can grow with patience.
TULA RASHI / LIBRAToday's Theme:
Connection feels uplifting today, but clear boundaries will matter more than polite silence.
Best Area:
Career flows best when you trust quiet instincts over outside noise.
Watch Out For:
Money stress can grow if you avoid a practical review.
Card Reading:
Justice is your anchor, while today's overall card, Three of Cups upright, blends fairness with warmth. It turns your focus toward friendship, support systems, and shared joy, while reminding you to keep emotional balance inside social situations.
General | Card: Three of Cups upright
Today feels lighter than usual, and people may be more open, helpful, or ready to include you. Three of Cups upright puts community, friendly catch-ups, and shared wins in focus. A WhatsApp family group update or a casual office chai break can bring useful warmth, not just small talk. Still, your Libra nature works best when joy doesn't become people-pleasing. Say yes where your heart is present, not where you're only keeping the peace. A happy day can still need honest limits.
Love and Relationship | Card: Four of Pentacles reversed
Relationships need breathing space. Four of Pentacles reversed in love can loosen a tight emotional grip, but only if you stop holding feelings in or holding someone too closely. If you're attached, don't test affection through silence, control, or subtle withdrawal. Speak plainly. If you're single, fear of vulnerability may be stronger than lack of options. Let one real conversation go deeper than surface charm. Openness doesn't mean oversharing, it means dropping the guarded pose that keeps closeness stuck.
Education and Career | Card: The High Priestess upright
Work benefits from quiet observation more than loud display. The High Priestess upright in career points to hidden information, unspoken office politics, or a strong inner nudge about timing. During a boss follow-up, listen carefully to what's implied, not just what's said. If you're studying, trust the chapter or topic your mind keeps returning to. You don't need to reveal every plan yet. A calm, graceful approach suits Libra well today, especially in meetings where everyone else is rushing to be heard.
Money and Finance | Card: Five of Pentacles upright
Money may feel a bit tight, or you may briefly compare your situation with someone else's and feel behind. Five of Pentacles upright is a reminder to deal with facts, not mood. Check a pending payment, delay a nonessential UPI payment if needed, and avoid spending just to feel socially included. If help is available, practical or emotional, don't isolate yourself. This isn't a day for denial. A small review of bills, balances, and priorities can reduce the weight quickly.
Health and Well-being | Card: Six of Swords upright
Your system needs gentler movement away from mental clutter. Six of Swords upright in health suggests recovery through transition, better sleep habits, and stepping out of draining thought loops. If the commute or screen time has been tiring you out, create a smoother evening rhythm. Lighter food, less doom-scrolling, and a quieter wind-down will help. Progress may be gradual, but it is progress.
Spiritual Guidance | Card: Four of Cups upright
Four of Cups upright turns your attention inward, especially if you've been emotionally present for everyone except yourself. There may be a blessing nearby that you've stopped noticing. Sit for two quiet minutes at your prayer corner and let stillness replace emotional boredom.
VRISCHIKA RASHI / SCORPIOToday's Theme:
Fresh energy wants movement, but steady boundaries will keep excitement from getting messy.
Best Area:
Spiritual grounding feels strongest through care, softness, and receiving support.
Watch Out For:
Career friction grows if you react to instability before checking facts.
Card Reading:
Death is your anchor, while today's overall card, Page of Wands upright, adds fresh fire to deep inner change. It encourages curiosity, initiative, and a lighter approach, without losing Scorpio's instinct for meaningful direction.
General | Card: Page of Wands upright
Something in you is ready to move again. Page of Wands upright brings a fresh spark, whether it's a new idea, a bold message, or renewed interest in something you had parked. During the commute or even while waiting at a traffic signal, your mind may suddenly connect dots fast. This is good energy for trying, asking, exploring. Just don't force a full plan too early. Let interest become action in small steps. For Scorpio, momentum works best today when intensity gives a little space to play.
Love and Relationship | Card: Seven of Wands upright
Love needs courage, not overprotection. Seven of Wands upright shows a need to stand your ground, but not every conversation is a battlefield. If you're committed, defend the relationship from outside noise, not from each other. If you're single, be clear about your boundaries without sounding closed off. A delayed WhatsApp reply doesn't automatically mean disinterest. Loyalty matters to you, but today asks for steady confidence instead of suspicion. Protect what matters, yes, but leave room for warmth and trust to breathe.
Education and Career | Card: Four of Wands reversed
Work may feel less settled than you'd like. Four of Wands reversed in career can show team mismatch, shifting plans, or a project environment that lacks proper coordination. An HR email, schedule change, or unclear handover could create irritation. Don't let temporary instability become a personal story about betrayal or failure. Stay practical. Clarify roles, confirm timelines, and avoid reacting to every wobble. If you're studying, create structure where the day feels scattered. Stability won't come from mood, it will come from better arrangement.
Money and Finance | Card: The World reversed
Financial matters need patience. The World reversed suggests unfinished loops, delayed closure, or a task that should have been wrapped up but still needs attention. Check subscription renewal dates, pending paperwork, or a payment trail before assuming something is done. Shortcuts can create repeat stress later. If you're waiting on money, keep expectations realistic and follow up cleanly. This isn't bad luck, it's incomplete handling. Closing one loose end properly will feel more useful than chasing five new money ideas at once.
Health and Well-being | Card: Eight of Cups reversed
You may be holding on to a draining pattern simply because it feels familiar. Eight of Cups reversed in health can reflect emotional stagnation, uneven rest, or reluctance to change a habit that's lowering your energy. If sleep, hydration, or food timing has slipped, don't wait for motivation. Start with one correction. Even a simple tiffin routine instead of random snacking can help your body feel safer and steadier.
Spiritual Guidance | Card: The Empress upright
The Empress upright softens your inner world and reminds you that strength also grows through care, beauty, and nourishment. A temple visit, fresh flowers, or simply eating with attention can become a spiritual act today. I receive support without questioning whether I deserve it.
DHANU RASHI / SAGITTARIUSToday's Theme:
You can get a lot done today, if action stays sharper than impulse.
Best Area:
General momentum is strong, especially where skill and confidence work together.
Watch Out For:
Love and career both suffer if you avoid an uncomfortable truth.
Card Reading:
Temperance is your anchor, while today's overall card, The Magician upright, sharpens focus and initiative. It channels Sagittarius enthusiasm into skillful action, helping big ideas become practical moves instead of scattered promises.
General | Card: The Magician upright
You have usable energy today, not just excitement. The Magician upright highlights skill, timing, and the ability to work with what you already have. A good idea during morning chai can become a real plan by afternoon if you stop waiting for the perfect setup. Messages, tools, contacts, and your own voice are enough to begin. This is a strong day for pitching, applying, organising, or restarting something that had gone cold. Just remember, confidence works best when it stays tied to follow-through.
Love and Relationship | Card: Ten of Cups reversed
Home tone and emotional alignment need attention. Ten of Cups reversed in love can bring small disappointments, mismatched expectations, or tension around family involvement. A family dinner may feel pleasant on the surface while something important remains unsaid. If you're in a relationship, don't cover discomfort with jokes or overpromises. If you're single, ask whether you're chasing the idea of togetherness more than actual compatibility. Warmth is possible, but it needs honesty about what isn't flowing smoothly right now.
Education and Career | Card: Two of Swords upright
A decision can't be postponed forever. Two of Swords upright in career reflects a stalemate, often created by too much thinking and not enough choosing. You may be torn between two options, two methods, or two priorities in your study timetable or workday. If a client call or deadline is approaching, gather the missing fact and decide. Waiting for zero risk will keep the block alive. Sagittarius usually moves fast, but today progress comes from sitting with the choice long enough to make a clean one.
Money and Finance | Card: Four of Cups upright
Money matters may feel emotionally flat, and that can lead to careless skipping over details. Four of Cups upright suggests a missed chance, ignored message, or boredom around budgeting. Check that bank message instead of postponing it again. If you've been adding items to an online shopping cart just for distraction, pause before checkout. This is less about shortage and more about disengagement. One practical review can reveal an option or saving that was already sitting in front of you.
Health and Well-being | Card: Seven of Swords reversed
Your body may need more honesty than heroics today. Seven of Swords reversed in health connects wellbeing with coming clean about what's draining you, late nights, too much screen time, irregular meals, or pretending you're less tired than you are. If sleep has been patchy, admit it and adjust the evening routine. Recovery starts when excuses stop.
Spiritual Guidance | Card: Two of Wands upright
Two of Wands upright widens your inner horizon. You're being asked to think beyond today's mood and look at the larger direction of your life with courage. Stand for one minute near a diya or window, breathe, and consider this quietly, where do I need a bigger vision than my current comfort?
MAKARA RASHI / CAPRICORNToday's Theme:
Truth, balance, and cleaner choices help you handle pressure without carrying extra weight.
Best Area:
Health feels steady when you direct energy with focus and routine.
Watch Out For:
Don’t stay stuck in dull patterns just because they feel familiar.
Card Reading:
The Devil is your rashi anchor, while today’s overall card, Justice upright, turns Capricorn focus toward honesty, balance, and clean accountability. It shifts intense drive into fair decisions, measured responses, and practical correction where something has gone off track.
General | Card: Justice upright
Today works best when you keep things simple, fair, and clear. Justice upright puts a spotlight on facts, timing, and responsibility, so half-decisions won’t feel comfortable. You may need to correct a small imbalance at home or work, especially if pressure has been building quietly. Don’t carry everything alone just to prove you can. A direct reply, a cleaner schedule, or one honest conversation can settle more than expected. If a boss follow-up or family duty lands together, handle both without drama and without postponing what already needs attention.
Love and Relationship | Card: Knight of Pentacles reversed
There may be affection here, but the pace feels flat or routine-heavy. Knight of Pentacles reversed can make a bond feel stuck, especially if practical responsibilities have replaced warmth. If you’re partnered, don’t let every talk become a checklist over tiffin, bills, or errands. Add some presence, not just duty. If you’re single, boredom may be making you dismiss someone too quickly or keep chatting without real interest. Small effort matters today, but it has to feel alive, not mechanical.
Education and Career | Card: Eight of Cups reversed
You may know something isn’t fully satisfying, yet changing it feels risky. Eight of Cups reversed often shows staying in a role, project, or study path longer than your heart wants, mainly from fear of uncertainty. That doesn’t mean resign dramatically. It means notice where you’re clinging. During the commute or between meetings, ask yourself whether habit is making the decision for you. A practical review of workload, goals, or next steps will help more than silent frustration.
Money and Finance | Card: Seven of Swords upright
Money matters need sharp attention today. Seven of Swords upright suggests checking paperwork, hidden charges, and unclear promises before you agree, transfer, or sign anything. If a pending payment, UPI payment, or account update seems slightly off, pause and verify. This isn’t about panic, it’s about being smart. Keep spending private if others are too curious, and don’t share financial details casually. Strategy helps, but keep it ethical. Clean records and careful reading will save you from an avoidable mess.
Health and Well-being | Card: The Chariot upright
Your energy can improve when you stop scattering it. The Chariot upright is strong for discipline, movement, and getting your system back under your control. If the day feels demanding, structure helps more than mood-based choices. Eat on time, stay hydrated, and keep your body moving even if it’s just a brisk walk between tasks. Emotional steadiness matters too. When stress rises, don’t push harder immediately. Direct your energy well, and your stamina is likely to feel more reliable.

item.content:encoded:
In this episode of Motley Fool Hidden Gems Investing, Motley Fool personal finance expert Robert Brokamp and Motley Fool employee Amanda Kish discuss:
- Maxing out tax-advantaged savings accounts.
- Tax-loss harvesting.
- Donating appreciated stock and new rules for deducting charitable contributions for 2026.
- Getting your withholdings right to avoid penalties.
- Roth conversions.
To catch full episodes of all The Motley Fool's free podcasts, check out our podcast center. When you're ready to invest, check out this top 10 list of stocks to buy.
A full transcript is below.
This podcast was recorded on Oct. 3, 2026.
Robert Brokamp: What you can do to lower your tax bill for 2026, this week on the Saturday Personal Finance Edition of the Motley Fool Hidden Gems Investing Podcast. I'm Robert Brokamp, and it's the first Saturday of the month, so it's time for the next installment of the 2026 Financial Planning challenge, which we're calling a year well planned. Speaking of the year, it’s now three-fourths over, making now a good time to do some fourth-quarter tax planning and make sure you are paying as much as you’re supposed to, but not a penny more. Here to answer eight questions that will help you optimize your taxes for 2026 is my Foolish colleague, Amanda Kish. Amanda, thanks for joining us again.
Amanda Kish: Thank you so much. I'm glad to be back.
Robert Brokamp: I will ask each of the questions. Amanda will explain why the question is important, and then I may add a thought or two. Let’s start with Question No. 1, which is: Are you on track to max out or at least meaningfully increase your tax-advantaged retirement contributions this year?
Amanda Kish: Great place to start. That is important because assuming that you're making pretax contributions, every dollar that you put into a 401(k), 403(b), or traditional IRA is $1 that doesn't get taxed this year. Just as a refresher for 2026, the 401(k) and 403(b) contribution limit is $24,500 with an additional $8,000 catchup if you are 50 or older. Then if you're between the ages of 60 to 63, there's an even higher super catch-up limit to be aware of. Then for IRAs, the annual contribution limit is $7,500 or $8,600 with the catch-up. If you have been contributing a flat percentage since January on autopilot, like most of us, now is really the time to actually run the math. Pull up your last few pay stubs, see what you've contributed year to date, and then compare that against the annual limit. If you've got the cash flow to do it, you can often increase your contribution percentage for just the last few paychecks of the year to close that gap. Some employers will also let you make a true catch-up lump-sum contribution before Dec. 31, so that is worth checking with your plan administrator or HR to see if that's possible.
Then, if you’re self-employed, of course, this question gets even more interesting because if you’ve got a SEP IRA, solo 401 (k), those have much higher limits. Let’s go into the tens of thousands of dollars, and the deadline for funding some of those extends past year-end and into your tax filing deadline. Ultimately, no matter what kind of plan you have, it's worth a quick check toward the end of the year just to make sure that you're on track to max out those contributions if possible.
Robert Brokamp: I'll extend this to a couple of other tax advantage accounts. Of course, there's the health savings account, which any contribution will lower taxable income this year. Then I'll also point out 529 college savings accounts, which don't really have an annual limit and a deadline per se, but most states offer a deduction on the state tax return for contributions to a 529. Every state has their own rules, so make sure you look into your state's rules. But if you want to take that, it does have to go in before the end of the year. If you want to take a distribution from your 529 for any qualifying expenses, you need to take that in the year that you incurred the cost. Question No. 2, have you reviewed your taxable accounts for tax loss harvesting opportunities this year?
Amanda Kish: Tax loss harvesting is the process of selling an investment. And again, this only applies to taxable accounts: selling an investment that is currently worth less than what you paid for in order to realize that loss for tax purposes. That loss can then offset capital gains that you've realized elsewhere in your portfolio this year. Then if those losses exceed the gains after everything's all totaled up, up to $3,000 of that excess can offset ordinary income such as your salary. Now anything beyond that $3,000 can then carry forward to future years indefinitely.
Tax loss harvesting matters most, I think, for people who are holding stocks or funds that have had a rough year, but it is also relevant if you have rebalanced a taxable account and realized gains, let's say earlier in 2026, as those gains might now have an offsetting loss sitting somewhere else in the portfolio. Of course, if we're talking about tax loss harvesting, I have to throw in there, the important thing that everyone needs to keep in mind here is the wash sale rule. If you sell a security at a loss and then you buy the same security or something that the IRS considers substantially identical within 30 days, either before or after the sale, that loss then gets disallowed for tax purposes. That’s a 61-day window that can trip people up from time to time, especially with ETFs or exchange-traded funds because two similar-sounding funds may be considered to be substantially identical, sometimes even if they are from different providers. If you do want to stay invested in that same general asset class after harvesting a loss, look for a similar but not identical fund to swap into temporarily.
Robert Brokamp: I will add that tax loss harvesting isn't just for stocks and funds; it really can be just about for any type of investment, including bonds which have had a rough year. In fact, the Vanguard Total Bond ETF, which is the biggest bond ETF in the world, is currently around $70 a share, so it's well below its all-time high of almost $90 a share set in 2020. You could do some tax loss harvesting with your bonds as well. Amanda talked about a couple of ways to violate the wash sale rule, and I want to highlight a few others. First of all, you can't buy that investment back during that 61-day window, and neither can your spouse. You can't do it in another account. You can't take the loss in your brokerage account and buy it in your IRA or 401(k) or your spouse do it. One way that people accidentally buy shares of the investment is through automatic dividend reinvestment if they hold it in some other place. That's something to keep in mind. Then one final thing to keep in mind is that there are lots of rules around options as well. You can't buy a call option on the investment, and there's some other options strategies that could violate the wash sale rule. make sure you know all of those.
Robert Brokamp: Let's move on to question number 3. Do you know whether your bonds, REITS, REITS being real estate investment trust, and other income-heavy holdings sit in the account type that makes sense tax wise?
Amanda Kish: Yes, this consideration is something called asset location, which is different from asset allocation. Allocation is about what percentage of your portfolio is in stocks versus bonds versus other categories. Asset location is about which account each of those pieces lives in. Taxable brokerage account, your traditional IRA, your Roth IRA, and all of these pieces and where you have your investments can meaningfully change your after-tax return without changing your actual investment mix at all. Brokamp, you mentioned bonds, REITS, other holdings like that that tend to generate a lot of ordinary income. Those get taxed at your regular income tax rate every single year. That's even if you never sell them, you never touch the cash, that income is going to show up on your 1099. If those holdings are sitting in a taxable brokerage account, you're paying tax on that income annually, year after year.
Now move the same holdings into a traditional IRA or 401K, and that income compounds tax deferred until you eventually withdraw it. Now, meanwhile, if we consider your more typically tax-efficient holdings, so these are things like broad market index funds that very rarely distribute large cap gains or individual stocks you may be holding long term, those tend to do relatively little damage sitting in a taxable account because you're not paying tax on that unrealized depreciation. The exercise here is simple. Pull up your account statements across all of your accounts, taxable, traditional and Roth, and look at what's actually sitting where. So if, for example, your bond funds are concentrated in the taxable account, and let's say your growth stocks are concentrated in the IRA, you may be able to swap the two around so long as you're not triggering any kind of unnecessary capital gains taxes to do that.
Robert Brokamp: I agree that most income-generating investments should likely be in your traditional IRA. I’ll just point out, though, that some bonds do have built-in tax advantages that you may lose once they’re in a retirement account. Municipal bonds, for example, could be completely tax-free, state and federal, if you do it right. Generally, you probably want to have those outside of the IRA. Treasuries are taxable at the federal level, but not state level. It probably still makes sense to keep them in your traditional IRA. I just want to point that out. Again, I think most experts would agree with putting the bonds in the traditional IRA.
The Roth is a little different. That's the tax-free account. It's the one you want to grow the most. Really, you would use that account for your highest-returning assets. Now, those are stocks, of course. Ideally, hopefully, you could choose what stocks you think will have the highest returns; you would put them in your Roth. Of course, it's not easy to do, but it's definitely a way to think about it and you would generally not hold bonds or cash in a Roth account. Let's move on to question number 4. If you give to charity, have you looked at giving appreciated stock or using a donor-advised fund instead of writing a check?
Amanda Kish: Yes. If you're planning to donate to charity, anyways, gifting appreciated stock that you've held for more than a year may be more efficient than giving cash. When you donate stock directly, you avoid paying capital gains tax on that appreciation entirely, and then you still get to deduct the full fair market value of the stock at the time of the gift, not just what you originally paid for it. Conversely, writing a check certainly gets you that deduction, but you do miss the CAP gain savings because you never had a taxable event to begin with. A donor-advised fund then takes that a step further. Here you contribute a lump sum. That can be cash, stock or other assets into the fund in one tax year, and then you take that full deduction immediately, even though the money doesn't need to go to any specific charity right away. Then from there, you can distribute grants to charities over the following years on your own timeline.
This is something that can be especially useful if you’re having an unusually high income year and you want to bunch several years’ worth of that planned giving into this year to maximize the deduction against this year’s income rather than spreading those smaller deductions across future years when your tax bracket might be lower. One more wrinkle worth mentioning: if you take the standard deduction most years, if you bunch several years of giving into a donor-advised fund in one year, that may be what pushes you over the threshold to itemize that year, which is where really a lot of the tax benefit of charitable giving actually gets unlocked.
Robert Brokamp: Yeah, I'll build on that by pointing out that to deduct the donation of appreciated stock, you do have to itemize. There's a limit on how much you can deduct in any single year for really any charitable deduction with excess amounts carried forward up to five years. But even if you can't take the deduction, you're still getting the tax benefit by donating appreciated shares because you're passing that capital gain onto the charity and they don't care because they're tax exempt. Then with the cash you would have donated to the charity, you can just buy back the stock immediately. You don't have to wait 30 days or anything like that, and you've set yourself to a higher cost basis. In my opinion, if you regularly give to charity, there's almost no reason not to donate appreciated shares rather than donate cash. It says we're talking about deduction, I do want to highlight two new rules that took effect this year. You can deduct up to $1,000 of charitable donations, $2,000 for married couples filing jointly without having to itemize.
But the money does have to go to a qualified 501(c)3 organization. Any donations to a donor-advised fund or private foundation is not eligible for this other deduction. Now, for those who do itemize, you're not going to be able to take quite the deduction you have in previous years because starting this year, only charitable deductions in excess of 0.5% of your adjusted gross income will be deductible for those who itemize. For example, if your AGI is $150,000, you'll only be able to deduct contributions in excess of $750. Let's move on to question number 5. Are you confident your withholding or estimated payments will avoid a surprise tax bill or penalty next April?
Amanda Kish: Yes. Unfortunately, the IRS generally expects you to pay tax on your income as you earn it throughout the year, and not all at once when you file annually. If you've had any kind of life change in 2026 and this could be a bonus that you've received, a new job, a home sale, freelance or 1099 income, a large capital gain from selling investments, there's a real chance that your withholding hasn't kept pace with what you'll actually owe. Here, it's important to keep in mind the safe harbor rule. What that means is that generally, you can avoid an underpayment penalty if you've paid through a combination of withholding and estimated payments, at least 90% of this year's tax liability or 100% of last year's liability. Although it's a caveat that increases to 110% if your prior-year income was above $150,000.
If you're not sure where you stand with your current withholdings, the IRS does have a free withholding estimator tool or this is something that your tax preparer, if you use such an individual can run a projection based on your income year to date. If it does look that you're behind, you basically have two levers at your disposal. You can increase withholding from your paycheck for the remaining months of the year, which the IRS will treat as if it were paid evenly throughout the year, even if it's a little bit more concentrated in Q4, or the other options to make an estimated quarterly payment directly. That fourth estimated payment deadline for 2026 is January 15th of 2027. You do still have time to true that up even after year end.
Robert Brokamp: I'll just add that there could be a benefit to doing this to making sure that you are paying enough taxes because if you experience some change, maybe your income was lower or you had something happen that will qualify you for a tax credit or deduction, it could be you're overpaying taxes. I know everyone loves to get a refund when they file their taxes, but the truth is you're basically losing the use of that money. It could be in your bank account earning interest, it could be in your retirement accounts growing. You definitely don't want to overpay if you can help it. I’ll just re-emphasize that if you don’t pay enough and you don’t fall under those safe harbors, you are going to pay a penalty and maybe interest. You definitely want to make sure that you get this as close to right as possible. Let's move on to question number 6, which is, if you're subject to required minimum distributions, have you planned this year's amount and whether a QCD makes sense?
Amanda Kish: If you are 73 years or older—or, Bro, I've sometimes heard you say 73 years or wiser—the IRS requires you to withdraw a minimum amount from your traditional retirement accounts every year. That's your required minimum distribution or RMD. That amount is calculated based on your account balance as of December 31st of the prior year. To calculate the 2026 R&D, you would look at the December 31st, 2025 balance, and that is divided by a life expectancy factor from IRS tables. If you miss the deadline or you withdraw less than required, the penalty can be pretty steep. That's about 25% of the shortfall, although that can be reduced to 10% if this is something that is corrected promptly. Keeping that in mind, here's something to consider. If you are charitably inclined, a QCD or qualified charitable distribution, lets you direct some or all of your RMD, that's up to $111,000 in 2026, straight from your IRA to a qualifying charity.
Now, that amount counts towards satisfying your RMD, but it does not count as taxable income. You compare that to taking the RMD yourself and then donating the cash afterward, where that distribution is going to show up as income first, and then the charitable deduction only helps you if you itemize. A QCD sidesteps that entirely and it's one of the few moves in the tax code where giving money away can directly lower your reported income, not just your deduction. But just as a note, the mechanics here do matter how you carry that QCD out. QCD has to go directly from the custodian to the charity. If that money touches your hands first, it no longer qualifies. If this is something you're thinking about, it's worth setting up with your custodian well before year end rather than waiting till the final days of December.
Robert Brokamp: I'll just highlight that what might happen is sometimes your custodian will send you the check, and you have to hand-deliver it to the charity. That's OK as long as the check is made out to the charity and not to you. That's just another aspect about doing the QCD. Getting back to RMDs, one thing to know is, if you're married, you have to calculate them separately from your separate accounts. You can't calculate the RMD and then just take it from one spouse's account or the other. However, if you personally individually have multiple IRAs, you have to calculate the RMD for each account, but it only has to be taken out of one IRA. 401(k)s are different. If you have multiple 401(k)s, you have to take the RMD from each. Then you might also have to take an RMD from an inherited account. That's a complicated topic. It depends on your relationship to the person who you inherited the account from and your age and various other criteria, but just know that you might be in a situation where you have to take an RMD from an inherited account.
ADVERTISEMENT: Spotify, it's Jay Sheri. Are you one of those media strategy people scrolling through spreadsheets, searching for an audience that pays twice as much attention to your ads than they do on social? Let me introduce you to fans. They're here with me on Spotify. Trust me, I know fans. They don't skip, they stay for hours. They don't move on, they manifest. They're not a demographic group. They're fans.
Robert Brokamp: Moving on to question number 7. Do you know which federal tax bracket you're likely to land in this year and whether that changes any moves worth making before year-end?
Amanda Kish: Your marginal tax bracket is really the thread that runs through almost every other tax strategy that we're talking about today. It determines how much Roth conversion will actually cost you, whether harvesting a gain versus a loss makes more sense, how valuable a charitable deduction is, whether extra retirement contribution is worth more to you now or might be worth more taken as income in a different year. The reason this deserves its own dedicated check is that a lot of people are estimating their bracket based on a typical year when 2026 might not have been typical for you. If there was something like a bonus, a promotion, layoff, a severance pay, a big capital gain from selling a business or a home, spouse, starting or stopping work, any of these things can shift you into a different bracket than you might assume from habit and from what has been true for you in the past.
These federal brackets are also adjusted annually for inflation. Even without any big life changes, the income level at what you cross into that next tax bracket has moved from last year. The practical step here is to pull together a rough estimate of your total taxable income for 2026. That includes wages, investment income, any one off events sometime before the year closes so that you're acting on real numbers rather than a guess. That single number is what makes questions like the Roth conversion or charitable bunching decisions answerable with any real confidence.
Robert Brokamp: You can use online tools to help you with these calculations. Most of the online tax prep providers also provide free calculators for folks, so, like TaxAct, H&R Block, Intuit. You'll find other calculators at other places like dinkytown.net has a 1040 calculator. I would say, actually, that's probably my favorite. It's the most intuitive to use. Just make sure that if you're going to use these tools that you choose 2026, sometimes the default is 2025. In some cases, they haven't come out with the 2026 tool yet, so you definitely want to use one that can calculate your tax bill for 2026. I would not use them and base my actual tax return on it. I think they're best used as getting a rough idea of what the consequences could be based on certain decisions such as, like Amanda said, doing a Roth conversion or contributing to a traditional account versus Roth, those types. What's the value of any kind of deduction right now? It can give you a rough idea, put some numbers to it and if you put it in the information correctly, it will give you an idea of what your tax bracket will be this year. Let's move on to our final question. Does a Roth conversion make sense for your situation?
Amanda Kish: This is a good one. A Roth conversion means moving money from a traditional IRA or 401K into a Roth account and paying that ordinary income tax on the converted amount in the year which you do it. In exchange, that money grows tax free from that point forward, qualified withdrawals and retirement are also tax free. There's no RMDs on the Roth side either, which can matter for estate planning as well as your own retirement income. The typical scenario where Roth conversion makes sense is in if you are in a lower income year, if you are between jobs in your early retirement before Social Security or pension income starts or any year where your taxable income is temporarily depressed relative to your normal working years. Converting while you're in that lower bracket means that you're paying tax on that money at a cheaper rate than you likely would either during your peak earning years or later in your retirement once RMDs and Social Security kick in and push your retirement income back up. That's not always universally the right move, though.
A couple of things to consider. You need enough cash outside the retirement account to pay the tax bill on the conversion. Using the IRA itself to pay for that tax really defeats a lot of the purpose of the exercise. Then equally important, converting a large amount can push you into a higher bracket for that year. You have to run the numbers, and it may make more sense to then do that conversion in smaller, more deliberate slices over several years rather than all at once. That's exactly where that bracket estimate from earlier becomes essential. Converting an amount that fills up your current bracket without spilling into the next one is usually as a sweet spot and a good target to aim for.
Robert Brokamp: I'll just point out that doing a Roth conversion doesn't just increase your tax bill itself. It increases your adjusted gross income, and there's a lot of things in your finances that are based on your adjusted gross income, such as your eligibility to take some deductions and credits, make Roth IRA contributions, maybe it could affect you if you're on an income-based student loan repayment plan, could affect how much you pay for premiums through the Affordable Care Act or through Medicare. You definitely want to have an idea of the whole picture when you're doing these Roth conversions. Amanda, what are your final thoughts when it comes to tightening up your taxes for 2026?
Amanda Kish: Thank you, Brokamp. I would say that I think for a lot of us, taxes are usually treated like an April problem. But the thing to keep in mind is that by April, most of your options are already gone, and you're basically just reporting what has already happened. If we're talking about December and where we currently are October, November, and December—that's a different picture. Every one of these tax strategies that we've talked about represents a decision that you can still make for 2026 with weeks to actually implement it. Whether that is contributing more to your retirement accounts, harvesting a loss, gifting stock instead of cash, converting to a Roth, what have you. You don't need to act on all of these that we've talked about, but even identifying two or three that genuinely apply to your situation and following through before December 31st can make a real difference in what you own next spring.
Robert Brokamp: I'll add as the final note for me that everything we've talked about here is true for federal taxes, but state taxes can be different. In most situations, your state tax situation is going to be similar, but there are a lot of one offs. For example, we talked about QCDs being excluded from your income. That's actually not the case in New Jersey. New Jersey doesn't exclude a QCD from your income. There are other little things like that. Like if you have leftover money in your 529, you can transfer it to a Roth IRA. If you do it right, it's a tax free transfer on the federal level, but California, it's not tax free. Just understand what the rules are for your state. With that, that's the end of our show. I want to thank Amanda for joining us once again, and thanks to Bart Shannon, the engineer for this episode.
As always, people on the program may have interest in the investments they talk about, and The Motley Fool may have formal recommendations for or against. Don't buy or sell investments based solely on what you hear. All personal finance content follows Motley Fool Editorial standards and is not approved by advertisers. Advertisements are sponsored content and provided for informational purposes only. See our full advertising disclosure; please check out our show notes. I'm Robert Brokamp. Fool on, everybody.

Minka Kelly Shares Cryptic Quote About Moving On From a Soulmate After Dan Reynolds Breakup
Minka Kelly is speaking out in a cryptic post following her recent breakup.
The 46-year-old Ransom Canyon actress and musician Dan Reynolds were revealed earlier this month to have split up “recently” after four years of dating.
Two weeks after their breakup was reported, Minka took to Instagram to share a photo dump, and the last slide featured a quote about soulmates.
“Soulmates, or partners of destiny, can be people that come into your life and change your life. And ideally, it’s not about holding on to it, but understanding what they brought into your life – what did you learn and how did you change? It’s about seeing these people and these situations as a gift, as steps in your own personal development,” the quote reads.
Last summer, Minka opened up about how Dan “healed wounds” in her that “he did not inflict.”
“His benevolence, his priorities, his values, and his honesty are all rooted in love. And as a result, we all feel safe and at ease in his orbit,” she added at the time. “Thank you for loving me. Thank you for blessing my life in ways I never thought possible – but always dreamed of.”
Minka sharing a quote about soulmates comes on the heels of Dan being photographed hanging out with Chantel Jeffries last week.
If you missed it, find out more about Minka Kelly‘s dating history.

Key Points
- Micron's cyclical nature is being reduced via contracts it's signing with clients.
- Tight memory chip supply conditions will worsen further before getting better.
Micron Technology(NASDAQ: MU) has had a great year. It's up around 230% so far in 2026, making it the fourth-best-performing stock in the S&P 500 this year. Normally, you're supposed to buy a stock before it makes a run like that, but even after the run-up, I've decided to open a position in Micron.
Why? It seems as if some of Micron's old tendencies are a thing of the past.
Missed AI’s "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 15x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we’re only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »
Micron is taking steps to reduce its cyclicality
Micron makes memory chips, and the industry is known to be cyclical. There isn't much that separates one memory chip manufacturer from another, so Micron has no pricing power. You can see this in action when you think about purchasing an aftermarket thumb drive or upgrading your computer's RAM. All components are about the same, but what really matters is how cheaply you can buy them.
The market goes through demand cycles that go up and down, and when it's swinging up, times are good for Micron and its peers. But when it's a downturn, they're stuck with excess inventory and can't sell any new production, so the companies, and thus the stock, struggle.
Right now, we're amid the biggest memory-demand wave ever seen, thanks to the intensity of the artificial intelligence build-out. All available production capacity for both types of memory chips (DRAM and NAND, both of which Micron makes) is currently consumed. Every memory chip company has said demand far exceeds capacity, causing prices to skyrocket.
The fear is that this demand wave will eventually fade, leaving Micron in a much worse state than it is now. However, Micron is taking steps to reduce the severity of the eventual downturn. Micron has now signed several deals with its clients that set floor and ceiling prices for memory chips, which will stabilize the market. Furthermore, these are take-or-pay agreements, so Micron has locked in an estimated 35% of its revenue through 2030. That's a huge step toward ending the cyclicality of Micron's business, as Micron is now being treated more like a true supplier rather than just a commodity dealer.
Another development is that Micron is partnering with Nvidia to create an industry-first custom memory chip for its GPUs. This will completely shift Micron's relationship with one of the biggest memory buyers in the world, which is a great thing for Micron.
Overall, Micron has taken steps to steady its business and reduce its dependence on cyclical demand. But the question remains: When will the AI demand wave wrap up?
The AI build-out just got extended
Most investors point to 2030 as the year when the AI build-out may slow, but Micron just informed investors that a few of its clients signed deals through 2031, indicating a longer time frame. Furthermore, conditions will get worse before they get better.

Conditions in the memory chip market were terrible for buyers in 2026, with far more demand than supply. However, Micron's management team noted that conditions will worsen still further in 2027 and 2028 due to lack of supply. While Micron is working on getting new production capacity running, it won't be until mid-2027 and into 2028 before significant supply is available. That means another couple of years of strong revenue growth, even after how much it grew in 2026.
All of this adds up to a stock that should behave like a normal big tech stock at least through the end of the decade. While I'm a long-term investor, the market is much more short-sighted, so that gives me plenty of time to invest in a company that's bound to continue growing as the AI build-out intensifies. I'm happy to own Micron shares and believe they will be highly profitable over the next few years.
But I'll also be keeping a close eye on memory chip market conditions, and if they deteriorate, I'll be moving on from the stock.

item.content:encoded:
Kimberly Guilfoyle may have announced her resignation Tuesday as U.S. ambassador to Greece over an expanding corruption scandal. But so far she hasn’t left.
The disgraced, short-lived diplomat has yet to vacate the elegant, official ambassador’s residence in Athens, the Daily Mail reported. Guilfoyle is “gripped by the mounting paranoia” that accompanied her desperate scramble to save her job, the Daily Mail also reported.
The New York Post, however, said that the former San Francisco prosecutor, conservative firebrand and one-time member of President Trump’s inner circle will soon pack up and return to the United States, probably to Florida.
And, in the wake of her dramatic downfall, Guilfoyle is considering whether to get even with members of the Trump family, including her ex-fiancé Donald Trump Jr., for appearing to turn their backs on her, the Daily Mail reported. She could do so by revealing family secrets she has recorded in a “secret burn book.”
Outside the White House Tuesday, Trump seemed eager to distance himself from his oldest son’s ex-girlfriend by denying a reporter’s assertion that she was “almost a member of his family.”
“No, she wasn’t a member of my family,” Trump said. “She, I guess, dated my son a long time ago.”
But Trump’s attempts to downplay Guilfoyle’s closeness to him and his family won’t stop her from “threatening” to release contents of the diary that Trump family insiders are dubbing “The Devil Wears MAGA,” the Daily Mail reported.
“Having her back in America would be a nightmare,” one source told the Daily Mail. “Kimberly knows where the bodies are buried. She knows the people, the secrets, the fights, the relationships. Nobody wants an angry Kimberly back home with nothing to lose.”
The 57-year-old ex-wife of California Gov. Gavin Newsom became a fixture in Trump’s inner circle after she began dating Trump Jr. in 2018, during his father’s first term. Together, Guilfoyle and Trump Jr. became a MAGA power couple and known as two of Trump’s visible supporters and fundraisers. They became engaged in late 2020 — after she gave a notoriously loud and enthusiastic speech on behalf of Trump at the 2020 Republican National Convention and before she joined the president in pushing his false claims of election fraud at his Jan. 6, 2021 rally, which led to the attack on the U.S. Capitol.
Even after Guilfoyle and Trump Jr. broke off their engagement in late 2024, and he began dating his future wife, Bettina Anderson, the former Fox News host appeared to maintain close ties to the Trump family, the Daily Mail reported. News of the breakup came around the same time that Trump nominated her to become ambassador.
But Guilfoyle’s stint as ambassador only lasted only 11 months before reporting by the Wall Street Journal and the Daily Mail revealed that she had allegedly been using her position for personal gain and engaged in alleged misconduct, in order to enjoy a lavish lifestyle while working for the U.S. government.
The alleged misconduct that garnered the biggest headlines involved claims by Erik Deters, a prominent former MAGA donor from northern Kentucky. Deters shared Signal text messages with the Wall Street Journal that showed Guilfoyle begged him to pay her $100,000 American Express bill ahead of her Senate confirmation hearing, while she promised to help him get access to Trump officials who could help him with some legal and IRS business.
The White House on Tuesday confirmed Guilfoyle was asked to resign, following reports that Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio were “extremely pissed off” by her alleged antics. The State Department has launched a review of the misconduct allegations, while congressional Democrats want to launch investigations if they take power after the midterm elections.
In announcing her resignation on X, Guilfoyle expressed her “unwavering gratitude and respect” for President Trump and said she will always be his “loyal supporter.”
She also insisted the accusations were “false” and vowed to “vigorously defend my name, my reputation, and my integrity.”
But behind the scenes, insiders told the Daily Mail that there was an effort to keep Guilfoyle in her job in Athens and protect her from further scrutiny over her conduct as ambassador. That’s because, contrary to what Trump said, she was very much inside the Trump family and its political operation.
“Kimberly knows everything,” the insider said. Another source added: “Keeping Kimberly happy keeps Kimberly quiet.”
But other Trump family insiders have told the New York Post they don’t think Guilfoyle will “lash out.” That’s because she may find herself in need of a presidential pardon if her scandal leads to a criminal investigation and conviction.
“She’s gonna need a pardon and if she doesn’t behave she ain’t getting one,” a person close to the White House and the Trump family told the Post, shortly after she announced her resignation.
“If I were her, I’d probably shut up and hope for it,” a second person close to the White House told the Post.
As damaging revelations about Guilfoyle began to pile up in the Wall Street Journal and Daily Mail, Guilfoyle tried to hold onto her job and began calling administration officials and people close to the president, playing down these reports and asking for their support, the Wall Street Journal reported.
When the Journal published the story about her soliciting $100,000 from Deters, Guilfoyle allegedly told White House officials that the text messages cited by the news outlet were AI-generated.
Amid concerns over what Guilfoyle could reveal about the Trump family, friends of her ex-fiancé expressed relief that he got out of his relationship with her before these scandals hit, the Daily Mail reported. One friend even insisted that he never actually proposed to Guilfoyle. She, instead, bought herself and engagement ring and began wearing it — prompting him to allow her to release a statement announcing their engagement.
It’s believed that Trump Jr. actually ended his relationship with Guilfoyle months before they officially announced their breakup. Two months before the 2024 presidential election, the Daily Mail published photos of Trump Jr., 48, hanging out with the younger Anderson and reported that Guilfoyle had been “blindsided” by the news that he was moving on.
These Trump family insiders also said that Trump didn’t nominate Guilfoyle to be ambassador to Greece because she had expertise in European geopolitics or because she possessed particular diplomatic skills. “It solved a complicated personal problem,” an insider said. “Having her thousands of miles away worked for everyone.”
This story has been updated.
